item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 6, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your MJR Morning Brief.
Radio Hall of Famer DeDe McGuire is bringing DeDe in the Morning to Nashville. The nationally syndicated Urban morning show is joining Cumulus Media's 92Q. Broadcasting from K104 in Dallas, McGuire and her team deliver entertainment, humor and lifestyle conversations to approximately 90 stations nationwide.
Turning to television,
Nexstar Media Group reported record third-quarter revenue of $2.1 billion, up 78% from last year. The increase was driven by its TEGNA acquisition and record political advertising revenue of $317 million. Net income climbed to $250 million, while NewsNation viewership grew 9%. Nexstar also reported strong cash flow and continued paying down debt.
In radio news,
KHCB Media Group in Houston has named Vance Frusher Senior Director of Development. Frusher brings more than 25 years of nonprofit and Christian ministry leadership experience, most recently serving as Director of Advancement for TeachBeyond. He'll oversee fundraising, major donor relationships and donor engagement as KHCB continues expanding its Christian radio and digital ministry.
Turning to television,
Telemundo 49 Tampa is expanding its newsroom with two new Multimedia Journalists. Mariangeles Muñoz, formerly with Univision Tampa, has already joined the team, bringing more than a decade of experience. Two-time Emmy Award winner Trouper Diaz joins November ninth from Univision Colorado, bringing extensive political and community reporting experience. Both will contribute to Noticiero Telemundo 49.
In music news,
The CMA has announced its first performers for the 60th Annual CMA Awards, including Miranda Lambert, Cody Johnson, Ella Langley, Tim McGraw, Kacey Musgraves and Zach Top. The show will also feature a special tribute to Dolly Parton. Lainey Wilson hosts the November 18 ceremony, airing live on ABC and Disney+.
And finally,
Sinclair reported a strong third quarter, with revenue climbing 16 percent to 893 million dollars. Political advertising generated 136 million dollars, helping more than double adjusted earnings. Sinclair also raised its full-year earnings forecast and expects a record 455 million dollars in political advertising revenue for 2026.
For the latest media news, job openings, free tools and more, visit MediaJobsReport.com.
